answer: Divergent Commitment Ledger: each identity commits to a random 256-bit seed and must publish a distinct follow-up action per epoch. Enforcement: any two identities whose revealed action histories ever converge within a similarity threshold are collapsed into one, forfeiting all but one balance. Clones cannot diverge freely, so copying forces each clone toward the ledger’s nadir of zero marginal reward. An attacker pays one full seed commitment and ongoing distinct-action generation per clone, making a large voyage of copies cost linearly in real compute.
